questions.text: Your team is developing a generative AI model to generate images based on user prompts. The model needs to create high-resolution images but must also be capable of running on hardware with limited memory. What factor will most affect the model choice?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Model size and complexity

Model size and complexity will most affect the choice in this case. High-resolution image generation requires powerful models, but if the hardware has limited memory, the size of the model must be optimized. Larger and more complex models typically demand more memory and computational power, so selecting a model that balances the ability to generate high-quality images with efficient memory usage is essential. Reducing model size or complexity can help ensure it runs effectively on constrained hardware.

Incorrect

Compliance with copyright laws

While important, copyright compliance does not directly impact the hardware limitations of the model. This is more of a legal consideration than a technical one.

Fine-tuning capability

Fine-tuning helps adapt models for specific tasks, but the issue here is related to memory constraints, not task adaptation.

Responsiveness

Responsiveness is important, but in this scenario, the ability to generate high-quality images within memory constraints is the key factor, making model size and complexity more critical.

questions.text: You are evaluating a machine translation model by comparing its output to a reference translation. The goal is to measure how closely the model's output matches the reference in terms of overlapping words and phrases. Which metric should you use?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

BLEU

BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) is a popular metric for evaluating machine translation models. It compares the n-grams of the machine-generated translation with the n-grams of the reference translation to measure how much they overlap. BLEU focuses on precision by checking if the words and phrases in the machine‘s output are present in the reference. It's one of the most widely used metrics for translation tasks, as it helps determine how closely the model‘s output matches human translations. A higher BLEU score indicates better translation quality.

Incorrect

BERTScore

BERTScore uses embeddings from the BERT model to compare the similarity between generated and reference sentences at a semantic level. While useful, it is not as focused on n-gram overlap as BLEU is for translation tasks.

ROUGE

ROUGE is mainly used for text summarization tasks rather than translation. It focuses on recall rather than precision, measuring how much of the reference summary is captured by the generated summary.

Recall

Recall is a general metric used in classification tasks to measure how well the model identifies all relevant instances. It is not specifically designed for machine translation evaluation.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/build-a-multilingual-automatic-translation-pipeline-with-amazon-translate-active-custom-translation

questions.text: A data science team needs to prepare and clean large amounts of raw data before training a machine learning model. They want a tool to simplify the process of data exploration and feature engineering. Which AWS service should they use?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler

Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler is designed to simplify the process of preparing and cleaning large datasets for machine learning. It provides a visual interface for data exploration, feature engineering, and data transformation, enabling users to easily handle raw data before model training. With SageMaker Data Wrangler, the team can import data from multiple sources, visualize patterns, clean and normalize the data, and create featuresall within a single tool. This makes it the most suitable service for their requirement of data preparation and exploration.

Incorrect

Amazon SageMaker Feature Store

Amazon SageMaker Feature Store is a repository for storing and managing machine learning features, allowing consistent feature usage across training and inference. While it helps manage features, it is not specifically designed for data exploration or cleaning.

Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor

Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor is used to track and monitor model performance in production, detecting issues like data drift. It does not provide functionality for data preparation or feature engineering, making it unsuitable for this task.

Amazon Transcribe

Amazon Transcribe is a service that converts speech into text. It is unrelated to data cleaning, exploration, or feature engineering.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/data-wrangler.html

questions.text: You are using a generative AI model to create automated customer service responses. The model‘s responses vary each time, even when given the same input. Which limitation of generative AI does this represent?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Nondeterminism

Nondeterminism in generative AI means that the model can produce different outputs even when given the same input. This occurs because generative models often use randomness in their processes to enhance the variety and creativity of responses. This characteristic is particularly useful in creative applications, but it can also be a challenge in situations like customer service, where consistent responses are needed. Nondeterminism is a key feature of many modern AI models and highlights their ability to generate diverse outputs, though it may affect predictability.

Incorrect

Accuracy

Accuracy refers to how correct or reliable the AI's responses are. In this scenario, the issue is not that the AI produces incorrect answers but that it produces different ones, so accuracy isn‘t the primary concern here.

Hallucinations

Hallucinations happen when a generative AI provides responses that are factually incorrect or invented. This is not the issue described, as the focus is on the variability of responses rather than the accuracy or truthfulness.

Simplicity

Simplicity refers to how basic or straightforward the AI‘s responses are. The issue here isn‘t that the responses are too simple; rather, it‘s about the model producing varied responses each time.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/machine-learning

questions.text: A developer is trying to optimize the performance of a generative AI model by reducing its input size without losing important context. What process involves breaking down text into smaller pieces that can be used by a transformer-based LLM for more efficient processing?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Tokenization

Tokenization is the process of converting raw text into smaller units called tokens, which can be words, subwords, or characters. In transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs), tokenization is a crucial step for efficient text processing. By breaking down the text into tokens, the model can handle variable-length inputs and capture contextual relationships between different parts of the text. This process reduces the input size without losing important context, as it enables the model to focus on meaningful units of language rather than processing entire sentences or paragraphs as single entities. Efficient tokenization helps in optimizing the model‘s performance by making the computational workload more manageable and improving the model‘s ability to understand and generate human-like text.

Incorrect

Reinforcement learning

Reinforcement learning is a machine learning paradigm where agents learn to make decisions by performing actions and receiving feedback in the form of rewards or penalties. While it is useful for training models in decision-making tasks, it does not involve breaking down text into smaller pieces for processing by LLMs.

Fine-tuning

Fine-tuning involves taking a pre-trained model and adapting it to a specific task or dataset by continuing the training process. It helps improve model performance on specialized tasks but does not relate to reducing input size through text segmentation.

Model training

Model training refers to the overall process of teaching a machine learning model to perform a task by exposing it to data and adjusting its parameters. While essential, it does not specifically address the optimization of input size by breaking down text into smaller units for transformer-based models.

questions.text: A logistics company needs to forecast the demand for its services based on historical data and seasonal trends. Which machine learning model would be most appropriate for this task?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Regression

Regression is the most appropriate machine learning model for forecasting demand based on historical data and seasonal trends. Regression models predict a continuous output variable based on input data, making them suitable for tasks like demand forecasting, where the goal is to estimate a future value (such as the number of services required). By analyzing relationships between features such as time, seasonal patterns, and demand data, regression models can provide accurate predictions. Logistic companies often use time series regression models like linear regression, ARIMA, or more advanced techniques to project future demand and optimize their operations based on predicted trends.

Incorrect

Clustering

Clustering is used to group similar data points together based on their characteristics but does not predict future values. While it can help in understanding patterns in data, it is not appropriate for forecasting.

Classification

Classification models are used to categorize data into discrete classes, such as “high“ or “low“ demand. This approach is unsuitable for predicting continuous values like demand, which require a regression-based approach.

Reinforcement learning

Reinforcement learning is used in decision-making processes where an agent learns by interacting with an environment, often through trial and error. It is not commonly used for tasks like demand forecasting, which rely on historical data and trends.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/machine-learning/latest/dg/regression.html

questions.text: In order to ensure the quality of data being fed into an AI system, it is important to evaluate the datasets for missing or incorrect entries before they are used. What best practice would you follow to ensure high-quality data?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Data quality assessment

Data quality assessment is the best practice to ensure that the datasets used in an AI system are complete, accurate, and reliable. This process involves evaluating data for missing, incorrect, or inconsistent entries and ensuring that the data meets the required standards before it is used in training models. By conducting thorough data quality assessments, you can identify and rectify issues like missing values or outliers that might negatively affect the performance of your AI models. This step is crucial in ensuring the overall effectiveness and accuracy of AI systems.

Incorrect

Data compression

Data compression reduces the size of datasets for storage or transmission but does not check for or improve the quality of the data itself.

Data normalization

Data normalization involves organizing data into a consistent format, which helps with compatibility, but it does not evaluate the completeness or accuracy of the data.

Data augmentation

Data augmentation generates additional training data by modifying existing data, but it does not address the quality or correctness of the original dataset.

questions.text: To improve the accuracy of a foundation model used for language translation, a team carefully selects high-quality text sources, removes noisy data, and ensures all datasets are aligned with the task objectives. What is this process known as?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Data curation

Data curation refers to the process of carefully selecting, cleaning, organizing, and maintaining data to ensure its quality and relevance for a specific task. In the context of improving a foundation model for language translation, the team is focusing on high-quality text sources, removing noisy data, and ensuring alignment with the task objectives. This helps ensure that the model is trained on the most accurate and relevant data, which ultimately improves the model's performance.

Incorrect

Data governance

Data governance focuses on the overall management of data policies, compliance, and security. It's a broader term and doesn't specifically refer to the task of selecting and cleaning data for model improvement.

Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)

RLHF involves using human feedback to guide a model‘s decision-making process, but it is not related to the process of selecting and cleaning data for training.

Data labeling

Data labeling is the process of assigning labels or annotations to data. While important for supervised learning, it does not encompass the broader task of selecting and cleaning data for alignment with task objectives.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-caf-governance-perspective/data-curation.html

questions.text: You are developing an AI system that generates customer support responses based on input queries. The system should adapt to different languages and provide accurate responses. Which generative AI concepts should you focus on to achieve these objectives? (Select TWO.)
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Transformer-based large language models (LLMs)

Transformer-based LLMs are key to creating AI systems that generate customer support responses. These models are highly effective for understanding and generating human-like text in various languages. They use attention mechanisms to process long sequences of words, allowing them to capture the context and meaning of the input query. By training these models on multilingual datasets, the system can generate accurate responses in different languages, adapting to the needs of diverse customers. LLMs like GPT and BERT are widely used for this purpose.

Tokens and embeddings

Tokens and embeddings are fundamental concepts in generative AI. A token represents a unit of text, such as a word or a character, while embeddings are vector representations of these tokens in a continuous space. Embeddings help the AI system understand the meaning and relationships between words. By using tokens and embeddings, the system can convert language into a numerical form that the model can process. This is crucial for generating coherent and context-aware responses, regardless of the language being used.

Incorrect

Rule-based systems

Rule-based systems rely on predefined logic and are not adaptive to language variations or complex queries. They are rigid and less effective for dynamic or multilingual customer support responses.

Multi-modal models

Multi-modal models process multiple types of data (like images, text, or sound) simultaneously. While useful in certain contexts, they are not necessary for generating text-based customer support responses.

Classical machine learning algorithms

Classical machine learning algorithms, like decision trees or SVMs, are not designed for text generation or language understanding. They are more suited for structured data and do not handle natural language tasks as efficiently as transformer-based models.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/generative-ai

questions.text: A video game company wants to use generative AI to automatically create realistic 3D models of characters and environments, speeding up the development process. Which of the following generative AI methods would be best for this use case? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reinforcement learning to create game environments
Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for creating 3D models
Diffusion models for generating high-quality images
Transformer-based language models for text generation

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Diffusion models for generating high-quality images

Diffusion models are a type of generative AI that can produce high-quality, detailed images, making them suitable for generating realistic 3D textures and visual components in game development. While these models are more commonly used for generating 2D images, they can be adapted for generating components that contribute to 3D model creation, such as textures for characters and environments, leading to visually realistic outputs.

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for creating 3D models

Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are highly effective for creating realistic 3D models. GANs consist of two neural networks (a generator and a discriminator) that work together to produce realistic data. In the context of video game development, GANs can generate detailed 3D models of characters, landscapes, and environments by learning from large datasets of 3D assets. This method accelerates the development process by automating the creation of complex and realistic models.

Incorrect

Reinforcement learning to create game environments

Reinforcement learning is useful for training AI agents to interact with environments but is not designed for generating 3D models or characters. It focuses on decision-making and learning through actions rather than content generation.

Transformer-based language models for text generation

Transformer-based language models are optimized for text generation and understanding. While powerful for dialogue systems or game narratives, they are not suitable for generating 3D models or visual content.

Clustering algorithms for model generation

Clustering algorithms group similar data points but are not used for generating new 3D models. They do not have the capability to create new assets, making them irrelevant to this use case.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/safe-image-generation-and-diffusion-models-with-amazon-ai-content-moderation-services

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/gan

questions.text: A company needs to automatically detect the sentiment of tweets related to their brand. They want to classify the sentiment as positive, negative, neutral, or mixed. Which Amazon Comprehend feature should they use?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Sentiment analysis

Amazon Comprehend's Sentiment Analysis is a powerful natural language processing (NLP) tool designed to automatically analyze and categorize the emotional tone of text. It uses machine learning to detect whether a piece of text expresses positive, negative, neutral, or mixed sentiment. This feature is commonly used in customer feedback, social media monitoring, or product reviews, helping businesses gain valuable insights into how customers feel about their products or services. With its ability to process vast amounts of data, Amazon Comprehend enables organizations to identify trends and make data-driven decisions more effectively. Its integration with other AWS services also makes it easy to implement within broader analytics workflows.

Incorrect

Syntax analysis

Syntax analysis identifies the part of speech (nouns, verbs, etc.) in a text but does not classify sentiment. It focuses on the structure of the language rather than the emotions expressed.

Named entity recognition

Named entity recognition (NER) detects and classifies entities like names, dates, or locations in text. While it is useful for identifying important information, it does not provide sentiment classification.

Keyphrase extraction

Keyphrase extraction identifies the most relevant phrases in a text but does not provide insight into the sentiment or emotional tone of the content.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/how-sentiment.html

questions.text: You are working on a customer service AI solution that needs to guide users through a series of interactions, such as checking account balances, resolving issues, and offering promotions. How can agents for Amazon Bedrock help in such a multi-step task?

options.text: Agents will prioritize tasks sequentially and assign models for each step in the workflow.
Agents will manually assign tasks to different service representatives for human handling.
Agents will act as individual models for each task, requiring no additional orchestration.
Agents provide a way to define dependencies between tasks and ensure that models complete their assigned tasks in the correct order.

questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Agents provide a way to define dependencies between tasks and ensure that models complete their assigned tasks in the correct order.

In Amazon Bedrock, agents can help manage complex multi-step workflows by defining dependencies between tasks. This ensures that the right model or service is called at the right time to complete each task in the correct sequence. For instance, an agent can guide users through checking account balances, resolving issues, and offering promotions, ensuring that each interaction is handled properly and that tasks are processed in the correct order. This orchestration makes it easier to manage complex workflows with minimal manual intervention.

Incorrect

Agents will act as individual models for each task, requiring no additional orchestration.

Agents in Amazon Bedrock do not act as individual models. Instead, they orchestrate the workflow, ensuring tasks are completed in the correct order and handled by the appropriate models.

Agents will prioritize tasks sequentially and assign models for each step in the workflow.

Although agents help manage tasks, they don‘t just prioritize tasks sequentially. They ensure the correct task flow by defining dependencies and orchestrating the right models, not simply assigning tasks step by step.

Agents will manually assign tasks to different service representatives for human handling.

Agents in Amazon Bedrock are designed to manage workflows autonomously using AI models, not to manually assign tasks to human representatives.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agents

questions.text: A team is developing an AI model for generating legal documents. To ensure the model understands that it should generate formal language, they need to provide specific directives in the prompt. What type of prompt engineering construct should they use?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Instruction prompting

Instruction prompting involves providing the AI model with explicit instructions on how to perform a task. By giving clear directives in the prompt, you guide the model to generate responses that meet specific requirements, such as using formal language for legal documents. This technique helps the model understand the desired tone, style, and content structure. For example, starting your prompt with “Draft a formal legal document that includes…“ tells the model exactly what you expect. Instruction prompting is effective because it leverages the model‘s ability to follow detailed instructions, ensuring the output aligns with your objectives.

Incorrect

Model latent space

Model latent space refers to the internal representations and features learned by the AI model during training. Users typically don‘t interact with or modify the latent space directly when crafting prompts.

Few-shot prompting

Few-shot prompting provides the model with a few examples to learn from within the prompt. While this can guide style and format, it relies on examples rather than explicit instructions for formality.

Negative prompting

Negative prompting tells the model what to avoid in its response. It focuses on prohibiting certain content but doesn‘t provide specific directives to achieve a formal tone.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-engineering-guidelines.html

questions.text: A healthcare company wants to train multiple machine learning models using different algorithms to predict patient outcomes. They are looking for a feature that can automatically try different algorithms and find the best-performing model. Which Amazon SageMaker feature can help with this?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Amazon SageMaker Autopilot

Amazon SageMaker Autopilot automates the process of training and evaluating multiple machine learning models using different algorithms. It automatically tries a variety of models and hyperparameter combinations to find the best-performing one based on the dataset provided. Autopilot also provides detailed insights into the model performance and allows for further fine-tuning if needed. For a healthcare company looking to train models to predict patient outcomes, SageMaker Autopilot can significantly streamline the process by finding the most effective model automatically.

Incorrect

Amazon SageMaker Studio

SageMaker Studio is an integrated development environment for building and deploying machine learning models. While it provides tools for model development, it does not automatically try different algorithms like Autopilot.

Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth

SageMaker Ground Truth is a data labeling service that helps create labeled datasets for machine learning models. It is not used for trying different algorithms or finding the best-performing model.

Amazon SageMaker Feature Store

SageMaker Feature Store is a centralized repository for storing and managing features for machine learning models. It helps manage features but does not handle algorithm selection or model training automation.

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/autopilot-automate-model-development.html

questions.text: A data scientist is tasked with choosing the right data for training a foundation model to ensure it captures relevant patterns for their customer support chatbot. What is the most important consideration during the data selection stage?
questions.explanationHtml:
Correct

Ensuring data representativeness and quality

Ensuring data representativeness and quality is paramount during the data selection stage for training a foundation model, especially for a chatbot. Representative data ensures that the model captures the full range of customer inquiries, language nuances, and interaction patterns it will encounter in real-world scenarios. High-quality data free from errors, biases, and irrelevant information enhances the model‘s ability to understand and respond accurately to user inputs. By focusing on data that accurately reflects the target user base and interaction types, the data scientist can train a model that delivers effective and reliable customer support, leading to improved user satisfaction and operational efficiency.

Incorrect Options:

Choosing the right cloud provider

While selecting an appropriate cloud provider is important for scalability, performance, and cost considerations, it is not the most critical factor during the data selection stage. The cloud provider does not influence the inherent quality or representativeness of the training data.

Pre-training the model

Pre-training the model involves training on a large dataset to learn general patterns before fine-tuning on specific tasks. This step occurs after data selection and does not directly impact the considerations involved in choosing the right training data.

Selecting a pre-trained model

Selecting a pre-trained model is related to model selection rather than data selection. While it can expedite development, it does not address the need to ensure that the training data is representative and of high quality for the specific use case of a customer support chatbot.

References:

https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/data-preparation
